3.19.s:
3.91
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi pakveṣṭanicayaṃ tava ..
brāhmaṇānāṃ śubhā śvetā kṣatriyāṇāṃ tu lohitā .. 1 ..
3.19.d:
3.91
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि पक्वेष्टनिचयं तव ॥
ब्राह्मणानां शुभा श्वेता क्षत्रियाणां तु लोहिता ॥ 1 ॥
3.19.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Hereafter I shall explain to you the laying of baked bricks. / White [earth] is auspicious for brahmins, but red for kṣatriyas, 1

3.19.s:
mṛtpītā vaiśyajātīnāṃ kṛṣṇā caivāntyajanmanām ..
yasya varṇasya yā śastā tāṃ mṛdaṃ grāhayedbudhaḥ .. 2 ..
3.19.d:
मृत्पीता वैश्यजातीनां कृष्णा चैवान्त्यजन्मनाम् ॥
यस्य वर्णस्य या शस्ता तां मृदं ग्राहयेद्बुधः ॥ 2 ॥
3.19.m: yellow earth for vaiśya classes, and black for the lowest-born. / The wise man should take the earth that is recommended for each class. 2

3.19.s:
asaṅkīrṇācchubhāddeśādgṛhītvā śoṣayenmṛdam ..
śoṣitāṃ tāṃ vimṛdnīyātsaśaivālena cāmbhasā ..3..
3.19.d:
असङ्कीर्णाच्छुभाद्देशाद्गृहीत्वा शोषयेन्मृदम् ॥
शोषितां तां विमृद्नीयात्सशैवालेन चाम्भसा ॥3॥
3.19.m: Taking the earth from an unpolluted, auspicious spot, he should dry it; / and having dried it, he should knead it with water mixed with moss. 3

3.19.s:
hastadīrgheṇa yantreṇa tadardhavistṛtena ca ..
tadardhamucchritenātha kartavyā veṣṭakā matāḥ .. 4..
3.19.d:
हस्तदीर्घेण यन्त्रेण तदर्धविस्तृतेन च ॥
तदर्धमुच्छ्रितेनाथ कर्तव्या वेष्टका मताः ॥ 4॥
3.19.m: With a mould one cubit long, half that in width, / and half of that in height, bricks should be made. 4

3.19.s:
ātape tāstathā śuṣkā vipacennṛpasattama ..
kāṣṭhairasārairbhūpāla gokarīṣaistṛṇaistathā .. 5 ..
3.19.d:
आतपे तास्तथा शुष्का विपचेन्नृपसत्तम ॥
काष्ठैरसारैर्भूपाल गोकरीषैस्तृणैस्तथा ॥ 5 ॥
3.19.m: Thus dried in the sun, O best of kings, he should bake them / with poor-quality wood, O king, with cow-dung, and with grass. 5

3.19.s:
mṛdunā nṛpa pākena na śāntyarthaṃ pacecca tāḥ ..
apakvāṃśca na saṃgrāhyā na vilīnāḥ kathañcana .. 6 ..
3.19.d:
मृदुना नृप पाकेन न शान्त्यर्थं पचेच्च ताः ॥
अपक्वांश्च न संग्राह्या न विलीनाः कथञ्चन ॥ 6 ॥
3.19.m: He should bake them with a gentle fire, O king, not baking them to destruction. / Those unbaked should not be accepted, nor those melted down in any way. 6

3.19.s:
tāsāmatyarthapakvānāṃ bhaṅgo bhavati rūpake ..
bhavantyasārāścāpakvā vilīnāḥ kardanāśadāḥ .. 7 ..
3.19.d:
तासामत्यर्थपक्वानां भङ्गो भवति रूपके ॥
भवन्त्यसाराश्चापक्वा विलीनाः कर्दनाशदाः ॥ 7 ॥
3.19.m: Of those baked excessively, breakage occurs in the structure; / and the unbaked are frail, while the melted ones cause the destruction of the work. 7

3.19.s:
iṣṭakānicaye vahniṃ yo naraḥ saṃprayacchati ..
somavikrayiṇā tulyaḥ sa tu pāpaḥ prakīrtitaḥ .. 8 ..
3.19.d:
इष्टकानिचये वह्निं यो नरः संप्रयच्छति ॥
सोमविक्रयिणा तुल्यः स तु पापः प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 8 ॥
3.19.m: A man who applies fire to a kiln of bricks— / he is proclaimed a sinner, equal to a seller of Soma. 8

3.19.s:
tasmācchuddhena mūlena tatrāgniṃ dāpayennaraḥ ..
vartamānamukhaḥ satyaṃ saṃvibhajya prayatnataḥ .. 9 ..
3.19.d:
तस्माच्छुद्धेन मूलेन तत्राग्निं दापयेन्नरः ॥
वर्तमानमुखः सत्यं संविभज्य प्रयत्नतः ॥ 9 ॥
3.19.m: Therefore, a man should apply fire there through an uncorrupted source, / truly turning his face toward it and distributing [it] with care. 9

3.19.s:
pakvāstu śītalībhūtāḥ svānurūpaistvarūpakaiḥ ..
samyaksaṃyojitā yojyā yathāsthāne narādhipa .. 3.91.10 ..
3.19.d:
पक्वास्तु शीतलीभूताः स्वानुरूपैस्त्वरूपकैः ॥
सम्यक्संयोजिता योज्या यथास्थाने नराधिप ॥ 3.91.10 ॥
3.19.m: When baked and cooled down, they are properly joined with suitable forms / and are to be laid in their proper place, O ruler of men. 10

3.19.s:
iṣṭakāsañcaye naivamekaikaṃ rūpakaṃ budhaḥ ..
darśayettu suyuktena yamasyājñāṃ vijānatā .. 11 ..
3.19.d:
इष्टकासञ्चये नैवमेकैकं रूपकं बुधः ॥
दर्शयेत्तु सुयुक्तेन यमस्याज्ञां विजानता ॥ 11 ॥
3.19.m: In laying the bricks, the wise man should not display each single figure, / well-applied, knowing the command of Yama. 11

3.19.s:
evaṃ rūpakavinyāsaṃ śilāsvapi vidhīyate..
evaṃ suyuktyā kurvaṃti kāṣṭhasaṃghātakaṃ tathā .. 12 ..
3.19.d:
एवं रूपकविन्यासं शिलास्वपि विधीयते॥
एवं सुयुक्त्या कुर्वंति काष्ठसंघातकं तथा ॥ 12 ॥
3.19.m: In this manner, the placement of figures is prescribed also for stones; / in this manner, with good skill, they also make a joinery of timbers. 12

3.19.s:
kāṣṭhānāmāyasaṃ bandhaṃ samyakkāryaṃ vijānatā ..
iṣṭakānāmapakvānāṃ paṅkabandho vidhīyate ..13..
3.19.d:
काष्ठानामायसं बन्धं सम्यक्कार्यं विजानता ॥
इष्टकानामपक्वानां पङ्कबन्धो विधीयते ॥13॥
3.19.m: One who knows should properly make an iron bonding of timbers; / a mud bonding is prescribed for unbaked bricks. 13

3.19.s:
iṣṭakānāṃ tu pakvānāṃ śilānāṃ ca narādhipa ..
bandhaḥ kāryaḥ prayatnena vajralepakṛtaḥ śubhaḥ .. 14 ..
3.19.d:
इष्टकानां तु पक्वानां शिलानां च नराधिप ॥
बन्धः कार्यः प्रयत्नेन वज्रलेपकृतः शुभः ॥ 14 ॥
3.19.m: For baked bricks and for stones, O ruler of men, / an auspicious bonding should be made with care using adamantine paste. 14

3.19.s:
pakveṣṭakānāṃ racanā mayoktā sudhānvitā saiva bhavennarendra ..
sudhāśilānāṃ tridaśādhivāse sudhāśilā naiva gṛheṣu deyā ..15..
3.92
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi vajralepavidhiṃ tava ..
bindukāṃśca kapitthāṃśca āmrānsaṃhṛtya yatnataḥ .. 1 ..
śālmalīnāṃ tathā puṣpaṃ sallakībījameva ca ..
dhanuṣaśca tathā kalkaṃ vacāṃ ca manujeśvara .. 2..
eteṣāṃ samavetānāṃ samānāṃ manujottama ..
toyamaṣṭaguṇaṃ kvāthamaṣṭabhāgā vaśeṣitam .. 3 ..
tatastatra kṣipeddravyaṃ śuṇu tacca samāsataḥ ..
mallakīnāṃ tu vinyāsaṃ vatsalasya ca guggulam..4..
bhallātakāni bilvāni kurmuruṃ sarjameva ca ..
atasīṃ vasutapto'yaṃ vajralepaḥ prakīrtitaḥ .. 5 ..
lākṣāṃ ca kundaruṃ caiva gṛhadhūmaṃ tathaiva ca ..
kapitthabilvamadhyāni tathā nāgaphalaṃ nṛpa .. 6 ..
3.19.d:
पक्वेष्टकानां रचना मयोक्ता सुधान्विता सैव भवेन्नरेन्द्र ॥
सुधाशिलानां त्रिदशाधिवासे सुधाशिला नैव गृहेषु देया ॥15॥
3.92
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि वज्रलेपविधिं तव ॥
बिन्दुकांश्च कपित्थांश्च आम्रान्संहृत्य यत्नतः ॥ 1 ॥
शाल्मलीनां तथा पुष्पं सल्लकीबीजमेव च ॥
धनुषश्च तथा कल्कं वचां च मनुजेश्वर ॥ 2॥
एतेषां समवेतानां समानां मनुजोत्तम ॥
तोयमष्टगुणं क्वाथमष्टभागा वशेषितम् ॥ 3 ॥
ततस्तत्र क्षिपेद्द्रव्यं शुणु तच्च समासतः ॥
मल्लकीनां तु विन्यासं वत्सलस्य च गुग्गुलम्॥4॥
भल्लातकानि बिल्वानि कुर्मुरुं सर्जमेव च ॥
अतसीं वसुतप्तोऽयं वज्रलेपः प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 5 ॥
लाक्षां च कुन्दरुं चैव गृहधूमं तथैव च ॥
कपित्थबिल्वमध्यानि तथा नागफलं नृप ॥ 6 ॥
3.19.m:
The laying of baked bricks described by me may be one accompanied by plaster, O king; / [and that] of lime-stones in an abode of the gods; lime-stone must not be used in houses. 15
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Hereafter I will explain to you the procedure for adamantine paste: / having gathered with effort binduka, wood-apple, and mango, 1
as well as the flower of the silk-cotton tree and the seed of the boswellia, / and paste of dhanuṣa and sweet-flag, O lord of men, 2
these being combined in equal parts, O best of men, / with eight times as much water, a decoction reduced to an eighth part [is made]. 3
Then one should cast the [following] substances into it; listen to that in brief: / an addition of mallakī, and guggulu resin of vatsala, 4
marking-nuts, bael fruits, kurmuru, and resin of the sal tree, / and flax; well heated, this is proclaimed as adamantine paste. 5
Lac, frankincense, and soot from the house, / the pulps of wood-apple and bael, and nāgaphala, O king, 6

3.19.s:
balāṃ ca madhukaṃ caiva kiṃjāpaṃ madanaṃ tathā ..
mañjiṣṭhāsallakaṃ sarjaṃ vajralepaḥ prakīrtitaḥ .. 7 ..
viṣāṇāni gavāṃ rājanmahiṣāṇāṃ tathaiva ca ..
ajānāṃ ca tathā carma māhiṣyaṃ gavyameva ca .. 8 ..
rasabiṃbakapitthāstu vajralepaḥ prakīrtitaḥ ..
aṣṭau bhāgāstu nāgasya kāṃsyabhāgadvayaṃ tathā .. 9 ..
rītibhāgaṃ ca kathito vajralepastathaiva ca ..
sudhāpakvā tataḥ klinnā gavyacarmasamanvitā .. 3.92.10 ..
khararomayutā rājanvajralepastathaiva ca ..
teṣāmekaikasaṃyuktāḥ kāryāḥ śailagṛhā nṛpa .. 11 ..
pakveṣṭakagatāścaiva sthāyino manujottama ..
vajralepayutā hyete bhavantyapi dṛḍhāstathā .. 12 ..
tiṣṭhanti sumahārāja saṃvatsaraśatānyapi ..
sahasrāṇi ca dharmajña cāyutānyarbudāni ca .. 13 ..
3.19.d:
बलां च मधुकं चैव किंजापं मदनं तथा ॥
मञ्जिष्ठासल्लकं सर्जं वज्रलेपः प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 7 ॥
विषाणानि गवां राजन्महिषाणां तथैव च ॥
अजानां च तथा चर्म माहिष्यं गव्यमेव च ॥ 8 ॥
रसबिंबकपित्थास्तु वज्रलेपः प्रकीर्तितः ॥
अष्टौ भागास्तु नागस्य कांस्यभागद्वयं तथा ॥ 9 ॥
रीतिभागं च कथितो वज्रलेपस्तथैव च ॥
सुधापक्वा ततः क्लिन्ना गव्यचर्मसमन्विता ॥ 3.92.10 ॥
खररोमयुता राजन्वज्रलेपस्तथैव च ॥
तेषामेकैकसंयुक्ताः कार्याः शैलगृहा नृप ॥ 11 ॥
पक्वेष्टकगताश्चैव स्थायिनो मनुजोत्तम ॥
वज्रलेपयुता ह्येते भवन्त्यपि दृढास्तथा ॥ 12 ॥
तिष्ठन्ति सुमहाराज संवत्सरशतान्यपि ॥
सहस्राणि च धर्मज्ञ चायुतान्यर्बुदानि च ॥ 13 ॥
3.19.m:
balā, madhuka, kiṃjāpa, and madana, / madder, sallaka, and sal resin: [this] is proclaimed as adamantine paste. 7
The horns of cows and of buffaloes, O king, / and the skin of goats, of buffaloes, and of cattle, 8
and juice of bimba and wood-apple: [this] is proclaimed as adamantine paste. / Eight parts of lead and two parts of bell-metal, 9
And one part of brass is also stated to be diamond plaster. / Then lime, boiled and steeped, combined with cowhide,
and mixed with donkey hair, O king, is likewise diamond plaster. / Stone temples should be built, O king, joined with one of these [plasters].
And those made of burnt bricks will also be enduring, O best of men; / for when joined with diamond plaster, these become truly solid,
and they stand, O great king, even for hundreds of years, / and thousands, O knower of dharma, and tens of thousands and hundreds of millions.

3.19.s:
sudhāvarṇena sarvatra lepaṃ dadyāttathā bahiḥ ..
tataśca tāṃ sudhāṃ dadyācchobhārthamarimardana .. 14 ..
vajralepavidhānaṃ tu proktaṃ samyaktayā tava ..
devāyatanamukhyeṣu tathā ca bhavaneṣu ca .. 15 ..
3.93
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .. ..
kṛte tu devāyatane vidhānaṃ nābhavatkṣitau ..
kaivalaṃ hi tadā hyāsītpratyakṣeṇa narādhipa .. 1 ..
pratyakṣeṇāpi dṛśyante tretā dvāparayorjanāḥ ..
devānāṃ pratimāḥ kṛtvā pūjayanti yathāvidhim .. 2 ..
gṛhe pratiṣṭhā tatrāpi tretāyāṃ tu pravartitā ..
dvāpare cāpyaraṇyeṣu ṛṣibhistu tataḥ kṛtā .. 3 ..
teṣāṃ sampūjanaṃ nityaṃ siddhaistu kriyate nṛpa ..
pratiṣṭhāmātrakaraṇānnirvṛtā ṛṣayastu te ..4..
kalau pravṛttaḥ sarvo'yaṃ pratiṣṭhākaraṇo janaḥ ..
jñānaṃ paraṃ kṛtayuge tretāyāṃ ca tapaḥ parama .. 5 ..
3.19.d:
सुधावर्णेन सर्वत्र लेपं दद्यात्तथा बहिः ॥
ततश्च तां सुधां दद्याच्छोभार्थमरिमर्दन ॥ 14 ॥
वज्रलेपविधानं तु प्रोक्तं सम्यक्तया तव ॥
देवायतनमुख्येषु तथा च भवनेषु च ॥ 15 ॥
3.93
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥ ॥
कृते तु देवायतने विधानं नाभवत्क्षितौ ॥
कैवलं हि तदा ह्यासीत्प्रत्यक्षेण नराधिप ॥ 1 ॥
प्रत्यक्षेणापि दृश्यन्ते त्रेता द्वापरयोर्जनाः ॥
देवानां प्रतिमाः कृत्वा पूजयन्ति यथाविधिम् ॥ 2 ॥
गृहे प्रतिष्ठा तत्रापि त्रेतायां तु प्रवर्तिता ॥
द्वापरे चाप्यरण्येषु ऋषिभिस्तु ततः कृता ॥ 3 ॥
तेषां सम्पूजनं नित्यं सिद्धैस्तु क्रियते नृप ॥
प्रतिष्ठामात्रकरणान्निर्वृता ऋषयस्तु ते ॥4॥
कलौ प्रवृत्तः सर्वोऽयं प्रतिष्ठाकरणो जनः ॥
ज्ञानं परं कृतयुगे त्रेतायां च तपः परम ॥ 5 ॥
3.19.m:
One should apply the plaster everywhere on the outside with the colour of white lime; / and then one should apply that white lime for beauty, O crusher of enemies.
The procedure for diamond plaster has thus been correctly explained to you, / for the foremost temples of the gods and also for palaces.
3.93 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / But in the Kṛta [age], there was no ritual prescription on earth for temples; / for then [communion with the gods] was solely face-to-face, O ruler of men.
Even with their own eyes people see [the gods] in the Tretā and Dvāpara [ages]; / having made images of the gods, they worship them according to rule.
Consecration in the home was also introduced then in the Tretā [age]; / and in the Dvāpara, it was then performed in forests by sages.
Continual worship of them is performed by the perfected ones, O king; / but those sages were fulfilled by the mere act of consecration.
In the Kali [age], all this people has set about performing consecration. / Highest is knowledge in the Kṛta age, and highest is austerity in the Tretā;

3.19.s:
dvāpare tu tathā jñeyaṃ pratiṣṭhā tu kalau yuge ..
devatāveśmapūrvāṇi nagarāṇi kalau yuge .. 6 ..
kartavyāni mahīpālaiḥ svargalokamabhīpsubhiḥ ..
rājā tu sarvanagaraṃ na kuryānnṛpasattama .. 7 ..
yo na rājā hato yuddhe sa puraṃ kartumarhati ..
rūpakaṃ ca sunāmākhyaṃ kuryādrājā tathāpyasau .. 8 ..
durgaṃ sarveṇa kartavyaṃ rājñā bhūpatisattama ..
bhūmidānādibhiryastu kuryātsuvihitaṃ mudā .. 9 ..
pratiṣṭhāṃ sakalāṃ kuryādanyathā pāpabhāgbhavet ..
tatkṛtāyāṃ surārcāyāmaniṣṭaṃ syātkalau yuge .. 3.93.10 ..
kṛtaṃ tu tadaniṣṭaṃ syājjanmāntaraśateṣvapi ..
kṛtatretādvāpareṣu pratiṣṭhākaraṇātphalama .. 11 ..
yasmātteṣu kṛtāmarcāṃ siddhāḥ sampūjayantyalam ..
kalau kṛtāyāmarcāyāṃ siddhapūjā na vidyate .. 12 ..
3.19.d:
द्वापरे तु तथा ज्ञेयं प्रतिष्ठा तु कलौ युगे ॥
देवतावेश्मपूर्वाणि नगराणि कलौ युगे ॥ 6 ॥
कर्तव्यानि महीपालैः स्वर्गलोकमभीप्सुभिः ॥
राजा तु सर्वनगरं न कुर्यान्नृपसत्तम ॥ 7 ॥
यो न राजा हतो युद्धे स पुरं कर्तुमर्हति ॥
रूपकं च सुनामाख्यं कुर्याद्राजा तथाप्यसौ ॥ 8 ॥
दुर्गं सर्वेण कर्तव्यं राज्ञा भूपतिसत्तम ॥
भूमिदानादिभिर्यस्तु कुर्यात्सुविहितं मुदा ॥ 9 ॥
प्रतिष्ठां सकलां कुर्यादन्यथा पापभाग्भवेत् ॥
तत्कृतायां सुरार्चायामनिष्टं स्यात्कलौ युगे ॥ 3.93.10 ॥
कृतं तु तदनिष्टं स्याज्जन्मान्तरशतेष्वपि ॥
कृतत्रेताद्वापरेषु प्रतिष्ठाकरणात्फलम ॥ 11 ॥
यस्मात्तेषु कृतामर्चां सिद्धाः सम्पूजयन्त्यलम् ॥
कलौ कृतायामर्चायां सिद्धपूजा न विद्यते ॥ 12 ॥
3.19.m:
and thus it should be known in the Dvāpara, but in the Kali age [the highest is] consecration. / Cities preceded by the temples of the deities in the Kali age
should be constructed by kings desiring the world of heaven. / But a king should not build an entire city [himself], O best of kings;
that king who is not slain in battle is entitled to build a town. / Yet that king should also construct an image bearing an auspicious name.
A fortress must be constructed by every king, O best of rulers; / and he who, with gifts of land and the like, joyfully carries it out properly,
should perform the complete consecration; otherwise he becomes a sharer in sin. / If an image of the gods is made by such a one in the Kali age, it brings misfortune;
that which is done would bring misfortune even across hundreds of other births. / The fruit from performing consecration in the Kṛta, Tretā, and Dvāpara [ages is great],
since the perfected ones abundantly worship an image made in those [ages]; / when an image is made in the Kali [age], worship by the perfected ones does not occur.

3.19.s:
tasmātsuvihitā kuryādbhūmidānādibhiḥ kalau ..
yena rājñā hato rājā nānyo yudhi bhavetkalau .. 13 ..
pratiṣṭhā tena kartavyā nagare pūrvanirmite ..
anujñāṃ nṛpateḥ prāpya kuyādanyo'pi yādava .. 14 ..
sthirāṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ gṛhyāyāṃ nṛpānujñānakāraṇam ..
parapraṇītāṃ yastvarcāṃ sa kuryātpunareva tu .. 15 ..
3.19.d:
तस्मात्सुविहिता कुर्याद्भूमिदानादिभिः कलौ ॥
येन राज्ञा हतो राजा नान्यो युधि भवेत्कलौ ॥ 13 ॥
प्रतिष्ठा तेन कर्तव्या नगरे पूर्वनिर्मिते ॥
अनुज्ञां नृपतेः प्राप्य कुयादन्योऽपि यादव ॥ 14 ॥
स्थिरां प्रतिष्ठां गृह्यायां नृपानुज्ञानकारणम् ॥
परप्रणीतां यस्त्वर्चां स कुर्यात्पुनरेव तु ॥ 15 ॥
3.19.m:
Therefore, in the Kali [age], it should be properly endowed with gifts of land and other [provisions]. / A king by whom [another] king has been slain in battle, and no other in the Kali [age],
should perform the consecration in a previously constructed city. / Having obtained the king's permission, another may also do so, O descendant of Yadu.
For a permanent consecration in a domestic [shrine], the king's permission is the cause. / But he who again restores an image installed by another,

3.19.s:
vidhānaṃ bhūmidānādyaṃ kuryāttatra na śaktitaḥ ..
dviguṇaṃ phalamāpnoti kulaṃ caiva samuddharet .. 16 ..
3.19.d:
विधानं भूमिदानाद्यं कुर्यात्तत्र न शक्तितः ॥
द्विगुणं फलमाप्नोति कुलं चैव समुद्धरेत् ॥ 16 ॥
3.19.m: and does not fail to perform the provision of land grants and so forth there according to his capacity, / attains double the fruit and redeems his family.

3.19.s:
kṛtvā suvihitāmarcāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yathāvidhi ..
iṣṭāpūrtena dharmeṇa naro yujyatyasaṃśayam .. 17 ..
3.19.d:
कृत्वा सुविहितामर्चां प्रतिष्ठाप्य यथाविधि ॥
इष्टापूर्तेन धर्मेण नरो युज्यत्यसंशयम् ॥ 17 ॥
3.19.m: Having made a well-fashioned image and consecrated it according to rule, / a man is without doubt joined with the dharma of sacrificial rites and public works,

3.19.s:
rājasūyāśvamedhānāṃ phalena ca narādhipa ..
kṛte tretāyuge rājandvāpare ca narottamāḥ .. 18 ..
3.19.d:
राजसूयाश्वमेधानां फलेन च नराधिप ॥
कृते त्रेतायुगे राजन्द्वापरे च नरोत्तमाः ॥ 18 ॥
3.19.m: and with the fruit of the Rājasūya and horse sacrifices, O ruler of men. / In the Kṛta and Tretā ages, O king, and in the Dvāpara, O best of men,

3.19.s:
āgacchanti nṛloke'sminsaśarīrā divaukasaḥ ..
nāgacchanti kalau yasmātsaśarīrāḥ kathaṃcana .. 19 ..
3.19.d:
आगच्छन्ति नृलोकेऽस्मिन्सशरीरा दिवौकसः ॥
नागच्छन्ति कलौ यस्मात्सशरीराः कथंचन ॥ 19 ॥
3.19.m: the gods come to this mortal world in bodily form; / since in the Kali age they never come in bodily form,

3.19.s:
āgacchanti pratiṣṭhāsu dvijairāvāhitāstataḥ ..
tasmātkalau prayatnena pratiṣṭhāṃ kārayedbudhaḥ .. 3.93.20 ..
3.19.d:
आगच्छन्ति प्रतिष्ठासु द्विजैरावाहितास्ततः ॥
तस्मात्कलौ प्रयत्नेन प्रतिष्ठां कारयेद्बुधः ॥ 3.93.20 ॥
3.19.m: they therefore come at consecrations when invoked by brahmins. / Therefore, in the Kali age, the wise man should take great care to have a consecration performed.

3.19.s:
arcāsthaistridaśairlokaḥ kalau sarvo hi pālyate..
arcāgatāśca gṛhṇanti kṛtadevapratiṣṭhitāḥ .. 21 ..
3.19.d:
अर्चास्थैस्त्रिदशैर्लोकः कलौ सर्वो हि पाल्यते॥
अर्चागताश्च गृह्णन्ति कृतदेवप्रतिष्ठिताः ॥ 21 ॥
3.19.m: For in the Kali [age] the entire world is protected by the gods abiding in the images; / and abiding in the images, having been consecrated as deities, they receive [worship].

3.19.s:
tasmātkalau prayatnena pratiṣṭhākaraṇaṃ hitam ..
yatnātsuvihitaṃ kuryādbhūmidānādibhissadā .. 22 ..
3.19.d:
तस्मात्कलौ प्रयत्नेन प्रतिष्ठाकरणं हितम् ॥
यत्नात्सुविहितं कुर्याद्भूमिदानादिभिस्सदा ॥ 22 ॥
3.19.m: Therefore, in the Kali [age], performing a consecration with effort is beneficial; / one should always make it well-provided with care, through gifts of land and the like.

3.19.s:
iṣṭvā yajñairyathā yānti mānavāstridivālayam ..
tathaiva rājan gacchanti kṛtadevapratiṣṭhakāḥ .. 23 ..
3.19.d:
इष्ट्वा यज्ञैर्यथा यान्ति मानवास्त्रिदिवालयम् ॥
तथैव राजन् गच्छन्ति कृतदेवप्रतिष्ठकाः ॥ 23 ॥
3.19.m: Just as men go to the abode of heaven by offering sacrifices, / in the very same way, O king, go those who have performed the consecration of deities.

3.19.s:
tasmātkalau pratiṣṭhānaṃ kartavyaṃ bhūridakṣiṇam ..
yatnātsuvihitaṃ kṛtvā bhūmidānādibhiḥ śubhā .. 24 ..
3.19.d:
तस्मात्कलौ प्रतिष्ठानं कर्तव्यं भूरिदक्षिणम् ॥
यत्नात्सुविहितं कृत्वा भूमिदानादिभिः शुभा ॥ 24 ॥
3.19.m: Therefore, in the Kali [age], a consecration with abundant sacrificial fees should be performed, / having made it auspicious and well-endowed with care, through gifts of land and other [grants].

3.19.s:
durge pratiṣṭhā kartavyā nagare ca tathā śubhe ..
nityamāpaṇavīthyagre nānyatreti narādhipa .. 25 ..
3.19.d:
दुर्गे प्रतिष्ठा कर्तव्या नगरे च तथा शुभे ॥
नित्यमापणवीथ्यग्रे नान्यत्रेति नराधिप ॥ 25 ॥
3.19.m: A consecration should be performed in a fortress, and likewise in an auspicious city, / always at the head of a street of shops, and not elsewhere, O ruler of men.

3.19.s:
grāme vā yadi vā ghoṣe nāsti yatrāpaṇaṃ nṛpa ..
tatrodyāne bahiḥ kāryā grāmamadhye na kārayet .. 26 ..
3.19.d:
ग्रामे वा यदि वा घोषे नास्ति यत्रापणं नृप ॥
तत्रोद्याने बहिः कार्या ग्राममध्ये न कारयेत् ॥ 26 ॥
3.19.m: In a village or in a pastoral settlement where there is no market, O king, / it should be built there outside, in a park; one should not have it built in the middle of the village.

3.19.s:
nadītīreṣu kartavyā vaneṣūpavaneṣu ca ..
sarasāṃ caiva tīreṣu girīṇāṃ śikhareṣu ca .. 57 ..
3.19.d:
नदीतीरेषु कर्तव्या वनेषूपवनेषु च ॥
सरसां चैव तीरेषु गिरीणां शिखरेषु च ॥ 57 ॥
3.19.m: It should be built on riverbanks, in forests and groves, / and on the shores of lakes, and on mountain peaks,

3.19.s:
upatyakāsu ramyāsu guhāsu ca viśeṣataḥ ..
eteṣu yānti sānnidhyaṃ sthāneṣu tridivaukasaḥ .. 28 ..
3.19.d:
उपत्यकासु रम्यासु गुहासु च विशेषतः ॥
एतेषु यान्ति सान्निध्यं स्थानेषु त्रिदिवौकसः ॥ 28 ॥
3.19.m: in delightful valleys, and especially in caves; / in these places, the denizens of heaven manifest their presence.

3.19.s:
jalāśayavihīneṣu deśeṣu manujottama ..
sānnidhyaṃ naiva kurvanti kadācittridivaukasaḥ .. 29 ..
3.19.d:
जलाशयविहीनेषु देशेषु मनुजोत्तम ॥
सान्निध्यं नैव कुर्वन्ति कदाचित्त्रिदिवौकसः ॥ 29 ॥
3.19.m: In regions devoid of reservoirs of water, O best of men, / the denizens of heaven never manifest their presence.

3.19.s:
tathā suragṛhaṃ kāryaṃ yathā vāme jalāśayam ..
purastādvā bhavettasya nānyathā manujādhipa .. 3.93.30 ..
3.19.d:
तथा सुरगृहं कार्यं यथा वामे जलाशयम् ॥
पुरस्ताद्वा भवेत्तस्य नान्यथा मनुजाधिप ॥ 3.93.30 ॥
3.19.m: A temple of the gods should be built in such a way that a reservoir of water is on its left / or in front of it; not otherwise, O ruler of men.

3.19.s:
samaṃtāttu jalaṃ śastaṃ dvīpe devagṛhe kṛte ..
yatra devagṛhaṃ kāryaṃ tatra bhūmiṃ parīkṣayeta .. 31 ..
3.19.d:
समंतात्तु जलं शस्तं द्वीपे देवगृहे कृते ॥
यत्र देवगृहं कार्यं तत्र भूमिं परीक्षयेत ॥ 31 ॥
3.19.m: Water all around is praised when a temple of the gods is made on an island. / Where a temple of the gods is to be built, one should examine the ground there.

3.19.s:
śvetā raktā tathā pītā kṛṣṇā varṇakramānvitā ..
kuśābhiśca śaraiḥ kāśairdūrvābhiśca tathā yutā .. 32 ...
3.19.d:
श्वेता रक्ता तथा पीता कृष्णा वर्णक्रमान्विता ॥
कुशाभिश्च शरैः काशैर्दूर्वाभिश्च तथा युता ॥ 32 ॥।
3.19.m: White, red, yellow, and black, according to the order of the social classes, / and covered with kuśa, śara, kāśa, and dūrvā grasses,

3.19.s:
madhurā ca kaṣāyā ca tathā tu lavaṇā ca yā ..
varṇakramāddhitā bhūmiḥ sarveṣāṃ śṛṇvataḥ param .. 33 ..
3.19.d:
मधुरा च कषाया च तथा तु लवणा च या ॥
वर्णक्रमाद्धिता भूमिः सर्वेषां शृण्वतः परम् ॥ 33 ॥
3.19.m: sweet, astringent, and saline [in taste]; / the ground is beneficial for each in the order of the social classes. Listen to what is further:

3.19.s:
kaṇṭakidrumasaṅkīrṇā śarkarāloṣṭasaṃyutā ..
aśubhrā viṣamā durgā savalmīkā tathā ca yā .. 34 ..
3.19.d:
कण्टकिद्रुमसङ्कीर्णा शर्करालोष्टसंयुता ॥
अशुभ्रा विषमा दुर्गा सवल्मीका तथा च या ॥ 34 ॥
3.19.m: covered with thorny trees, full of gravel and clods of earth, / unpleasing, uneven, inaccessible, and with ant-hills,

3.19.s:
mūṣikāvāsabahulā pipīlakaguṇānvitā ..
nityaṃ ca śakaṭacchinnā plutā yā ca purodakaiḥ .. 35 ..
3.19.d:
मूषिकावासबहुला पिपीलकगुणान्विता ॥
नित्यं च शकटच्छिन्ना प्लुता या च पुरोदकैः ॥ 35 ॥
3.19.m: abounding in rat holes, full of ants, / constantly worn down by carts, and inundated by sudden floods,

3.19.s:
aghātasūnā bhūmiśca bandhanāgārasaṃyutā ..
vasatiryatra dagdhā ca vidyutā vahnināpi vā .. 36 ..
3.19.d:
अघातसूना भूमिश्च बन्धनागारसंयुता ॥
वसतिर्यत्र दग्धा च विद्युता वह्निनापि वा ॥ 36 ॥
3.19.m: ground that is a slaughterhouse or connected with a prison, / or where a dwelling has been burnt by lightning or by fire,

3.19.s:
vasatāṃ dṛṣṭidoṣā ca kūrmapṛṣṭhā tathaiva ca ..
trikoṇā sragvihīnā ca śūrpākārā tathā ca yā .. 39..
3.19.d:
वसतां दृष्टिदोषा च कूर्मपृष्ठा तथैव च ॥
त्रिकोणा स्रग्विहीना च शूर्पाकारा तथा च या ॥ 39॥
3.19.m: possessing defects offensive to the sight of those who live there, shaped like a tortoise shell, / triangular, lacking beauty, and shaped like a winnowing basket,

3.19.s:
dakṣiṇena tathā nimnā nimnā pṛṣṭhata eva ca .
purāmbugrāhiṇī yā ca suśirā ca tathā nṛpa .. 38 ..
3.19.d:
दक्षिणेन तथा निम्ना निम्ना पृष्ठत एव च ।
पुराम्बुग्राहिणी या च सुशिरा च तथा नृप ॥ 38 ॥
3.19.m: And [ground that is] sloping towards the south, and sloping from behind, / and that which collects old water, and that which is hollow, O king,

3.19.s:
khātaṃ ca sumṛdā yatra pūryate na punastathā ..
khāte yatra kṛtaṃ dīpaṃ pramlānimupagacchati .. 39 ..
3.19.d:
खातं च सुमृदा यत्र पूर्यते न पुनस्तथा ॥
खाते यत्र कृतं दीपं प्रम्लानिमुपगच्छति ॥ 39 ॥
3.19.m: and where a pit is not filled again by its good soil, / and where a lamp placed in the pit becomes dim,

3.19.s:
mālyaṃ ca mlāyate khāte tāṃ bhūmiṃ parivarjayeta ..
khāte toyena pūrṇe ca yatra toyaṃ na tiṣṭhati .. 3.93.40 ..
3.19.d:
माल्यं च म्लायते खाते तां भूमिं परिवर्जयेत ॥
खाते तोयेन पूर्णे च यत्र तोयं न तिष्ठति ॥ 3.93.40 ॥
3.19.m: and a garland withers in the pit—that ground one should avoid. / And where water does not remain when the pit is filled with water,

3.19.s:
tāṃ bhūmiṃ varjayadyatnāddurgandhā ca tathāpi yā ..
prāgudakpravaṇā śastā snigdhā ca sudṛḍhā tathā .. 41 ..
3.19.d:
तां भूमिं वर्जयद्यत्नाद्दुर्गन्धा च तथापि या ॥
प्रागुदक्प्रवणा शस्ता स्निग्धा च सुदृढा तथा ॥ 41 ॥
3.19.m: one should avoid that ground with effort; and likewise that which is foul-smelling. / [Ground that is] sloping towards the east or north is commended, and also smooth and very firm,

3.19.s:
khāte'dhikāṃ ca mṛdyatra pūryamāṇe bhavennṛpa ..
dīpo na mlāyate yatra nyastaṃ ca kusumaṃ tathā .. 42..
3.19.d:
खातेऽधिकां च मृद्यत्र पूर्यमाणे भवेन्नृप ॥
दीपो न म्लायते यत्र न्यस्तं च कुसुमं तथा ॥ 42॥
3.19.m: and where, O king, there is excess soil when the pit is filled; / where a lamp does not fade, and likewise a blossom placed there [does not wither];

3.19.s:
toyaṃ santiṣṭhate khāte yatra kālāntaraṃ bahu ..
sā praśastā mahī jñeyā sugandhā susvanā tathā .. 43 ..
3.19.d:
तोयं सन्तिष्ठते खाते यत्र कालान्तरं बहु ॥
सा प्रशस्ता मही ज्ञेया सुगन्धा सुस्वना तथा ॥ 43 ॥
3.19.m: where water remains in the pit for a long time— / that earth should be known as praised, sweet-smelling, and of pleasant sound.

3.19.s:
bhuvaḥ parīkṣaṇaṃ kuryāddivase'tiśubhe tathā ..
bhuvaḥ parīkṣaṇaṃ yatra maṅgalyadravyadarśanam .. 44 ..
3.19.d:
भुवः परीक्षणं कुर्याद्दिवसेऽतिशुभे तथा ॥
भुवः परीक्षणं यत्र मङ्गल्यद्रव्यदर्शनम् ॥ 44 ॥
3.19.m: One should examine the ground on an exceedingly auspicious day. / Where, upon examining the ground, there is the sight of auspicious objects,

3.19.s:
śravaṇaṃ vā tathaiva syātsā śubhā syādvasundharā ..
na tāṃ rājanparīkṣeta praśastā sā prakīrtitā .. 45 ..
3.19.d:
श्रवणं वा तथैव स्यात्सा शुभा स्याद्वसुन्धरा ॥
न तां राजन्परीक्षेत प्रशस्ता सा प्रकीर्तिता ॥ 45 ॥
3.19.m: or hearing [auspicious sounds], that earth is auspicious; / one need not examine it, O king: it is declared praised.

3.19.s:
amaṅgalyaṃ tathā dṛṣṭvā śrutaṃ vā nṛpasattama ..

3.19.m: Seeing or hearing what is inauspicious there, O best of kings, / examination of the ground should not be conducted there, for it is indeed inauspicious.

शुभा मही यत्र भवेन्नृवीर कार्या प्रतिष्ठा भवतीह तत्र ॥

3.94
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
शुभां परीक्ष्य वसुधां तत्र कुर्यात्सुरालयम ॥
आदौ तां शोधयेद्विद्वान्दिवसे गुणसंयुते ॥ 1 ॥
तत्र देशं शुभं विद्वान्गोमयेनोपलेपयेत ॥
ततः सम्पूजयेत्तत्र देवदेवं विनायकम् ॥ 4 ॥
तथा च विश्वकर्माणं भाण्डं तदुपयोगि च ॥
पललोल्लपिका भक्ष्यकुल्माषौदनपर्पटैः ॥ 3 ॥
परमान्नेन सत्यैश्च पुष्पधूपानुलेपनैः ॥
पूजयित्वा च दैवज्ञं सात्त्वतं स्थपतिं तथा ॥ 4 ॥
भुवः संशोधनं कुर्याद्यथावत्पृथिवीपतिः ॥
तावत्संशोधयेद्भूमिं निजां यावत्प्रदृश्यते ॥ 5 ॥
तदा संशोधयेद्विद्वान्यावत्स्याच्छल्यवर्जिता ॥
ततस्तु पूरयेत्पश्चाद्दृढं मृत्तिकया पुनः ॥ 6 ॥
3.19.m:
Where the earth is auspicious, O heroic man, the consecration is to be performed there. / When performed there, O moon among kings, it brings welfare and self-prosperity to the maker.
3.94
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Having examined the auspicious earth, one should build an abode of the gods there. / First, the wise man should clear it on a day endowed with good qualities.
There, the wise man should smear the auspicious place with cow dung. / Then he should worship Vināyaka, the god of gods, there,
and likewise Viśvakarman and the utensils useful for that work, / with meat, cakes, edibles, boiled beans, rice, and parched crisps,
with rice cooked in milk, truthful words, flowers, incense, and ointments. / Having also worshipped the astrologer, the Sāttvata, and the architect,
the lord of the earth should properly perform the clearing of the ground. / He should clear the ground until its natural [soil] is seen.
Then the wise man should clear it until it is free of foreign objects. / Thereafter, he should fill it firmly again with earth,

तद्वर्णया तया शस्ता यस्य वर्णस्य कीर्तिता ॥
अशल्यया मृत्तिकया पूरयेत्सुदृढं पुनः ॥ 7 ॥
कृत्वा तु पूरितं देशं सुदृढं सुसमन्ततः ॥
सुसूक्ष्मशल्यज्ञानार्थं कुर्याच्छल्यपरीक्षणम् ॥ 8 ॥
यथा वक्ष्याम्यहं राजंस्तथा यत्नेन बुद्धिमान् ॥
यदि स्याच्छल्यसंयुक्ता शल्यमुद्धृत्य यत्नतः ॥ 9 ॥
पुनः सम्पूरयेद्विद्वान्यत्नाच्छुभमृदा नृप ॥
एवं संशोध्य भूमिं तु कुम्भं संस्थापयेत्ततः ॥ 3.94.10 ॥
शिलान्यासं तु कुर्वीत तत्रैवाऽह्नि चतुर्दिशम् ॥
पक्वेष्टारचिते कार्यास्ता एव तु चतुर्दिशम् ॥ 11 ॥
मृन्मये चेष्टकान्यासं कर्तव्यं न च दारुणे ॥
शुभे दिवसनक्षत्रे मुहूर्ते चाभिपूजिते ॥ 12 ॥
कुम्भाकारां शिलां कुर्याच्छैलदेवगृहे शुभम् ॥
अन्यत्र ताम्रकलशं सुदृढं यत्र संयुतम् ॥ 13 ॥
3.19.m:
with that of the color commended for whatever class has been declared; / with earth free of foreign objects he should fill it very firmly again.
Having made the place completely and very firmly filled, / he should perform an examination for foreign objects to discover even the subtlest foreign matter,
with effort, as I shall explain, O king, being wise. / If it should contain foreign matter, having extracted that foreign matter with effort,
the wise man should fill it again with good soil with care, O king. / Thus, having cleared the ground, he should then set down the pot;
and he should perform the foundation-deposit of stone on that very day in the four directions. / In a temple made of baked bricks, those [bricks] alone are to be placed in the four directions.
In an earthen [temple], the laying of bricks is to be performed, but not in a wooden one. / Under an auspicious lunar mansion on a good day and at a revered auspicious hour,
in a stone temple of the gods, he should make an auspicious stone in the shape of a pot; / elsewhere, a very solid copper pot where it is joined.

3.19.d:
चतुःषष्टिपदं कृत्वा समे स्थाने तु मण्डलम् ॥
कृत्वा तु देवतान्यासं तत्र मण्डलके द्विज ॥ 14 ॥
सर्वेषां वास्तुविद्योक्ता देवतानां यथाविधि ॥
श्रियाः सम्पूजनं कृत्वा वासुदेवस्य चाप्यथ ॥ 15 ॥
पूजनं मण्डले कार्ये वास्तुदेवगणस्य च ॥
विनायकस्य देवस्य विश्वकर्मण एव च ॥ 16 ॥
भाण्डानां च महाराज तथा तदुपयोगिनाम् ॥
गन्धार्घपुष्पनैवेद्यधूपदीपैर्यथाविधि ॥ 17 ॥
ओंकारपूतमाज्यं च जुहुयाच्छ्रीधरस्य च ॥
श्रियाः कृत्वा ततो होमं ब्रह्मणः कारयेत्तदा ॥ 18 ॥
ब्रह्माणं पुरतः कृत्वा वासुदेवगणस्य च ॥
मध्ये कृत्वा ततः कुम्भं शिलान्यासं तु कारयेत ॥ 19 ॥
ऐशाने तु ततः कोणे शिलां पूर्वं प्रतिष्ठिताम् ॥
प्रदक्षिणं ततो राजञ्छिलान्यासं विधीयते ॥ 3.94.20 ॥
3.19.m:
Having made a sacred diagram of sixty-four squares on level ground, / and having performed the ritual placement of the deities in that sacred diagram, O twice-born,
properly for all deities spoken of in architectural lore, / and having worshipped Śrī and also Vāsudeva,
the worship of the host of deities of the site should be performed in the sacred diagram, / and of the god Vināyaka, and of Viśvakarman,
and of the utensils, O great king, and of whatever is useful for it, / with perfumes, water offerings, flowers, food offerings, incense, and lamps, according to rule.
And he should offer clarified butter purified with the sacred syllable Om to Śrīdhara. / Then, having made the fire oblation to Śrī, he should cause it to be performed for Brahmā.
Having placed Brahmā in front, and also the retinue of Vāsudeva, / and then having placed the pot in the middle, he should perform the laying of the stones.
First, the stone installed in the northeast corner; / then, O king, the laying of the stones is prescribed in a clockwise direction.

3.19.d:
सूत्रन्यासं तु कुर्वीत तस्मिन्नेव तथाहनि ॥
यथानिवेशं कर्तव्यं प्रासादस्य सुनिश्चितम् ॥ 21 ॥
कृत्वा तु सूत्रविन्यासं नाधिकं तं तु कारयेत् ॥
नूनं मनुजशार्दूल कर्तुर्दोषकरावुभौ॥ 22 ॥
कुम्भस्य च शिलानां च ततः स्थानं विधीयते ॥
वटाश्वत्थकषायेण सर्वौषधिजलैस्ततः ॥ 23 ॥
ततोऽनुलेपनं कुर्याच्चन्दनेन सुगन्धिना ॥
आच्छादनं ततः कार्यं वासोभिः कुसुमैस्तथा ॥ 24 ॥
धूपं दीपं सुनैवेद्यं तेषां नाम्ना निवेदयेत् ॥
दक्षिणाभिर्द्विजेन्द्राणां ततः पूजा विधीयते ॥ 25 ॥
कालवित्स्थपतिः पूज्यो ततो राम विजानता ॥
ततः कर्ता जपेन्मन्त्रं स्थपतिं वाथ कालवित् ॥ 26 ॥
नन्दे नन्दय वासिष्ठे वसुभिः पूजया सह ॥
जये भार्गवदायादे प्रजाभ्यो जयमावह ॥ 27 ॥
3.19.m:
And he should perform the laying out of cords on that very same day. / It should be done with certainty according to the plan of the temple.
Having made the layout of the cords, he should not make it excessive; / surely, O tiger among men, both [defects] bring harm to the patron.
Then the place of the pot and the stones is prescribed. / Then, with a decoction of banyan and sacred fig, and with water of all herbs,
he should then anoint them with fragrant sandalwood; / then covering [them] is to be done with cloths and flowers.
He should offer incense, a lamp, and good food offerings in their names. / Then worship of the lords of the twice-born with sacrificial fees is prescribed.
The astrologer and the architect should then be worshipped by the knowing [patron], O Rāma; / then the patron or the architect or the astrologer should mutter the mantra:
"O Nandā, daughter of Vasiṣṭha, bring joy along with worship by the Vasus! / O Jayā, offspring of Bhṛgu, bring victory to the creatures!

3.19.d:
पूर्णेङ्गिरसदायादे पूर्णकामं कुरुष्व माम् ॥
भद्रे कश्यपदायादे कुरु भद्रां गतिं मम ॥ 28 ॥
सर्वबीजसमायुक्ते सर्वरत्नौषधैर्वृते ॥
रुचिरे नन्दिते नन्दे वासिष्ठे रम्यतामिह ॥ 29 ॥
प्रजापतिसुते देवि चतुरस्रे महीमयि ॥
सुभगे सुव्रते भद्रे इह काश्यपि रम्यताम् ॥ 3.94.30 ॥
अव्यङ्गे चाक्षते पूर्णे मुनेरंगिरसः सुते ॥
इष्टके त्वं प्रयच्छेष्टं प्रतिष्ठां कामयाम्यहम् ॥ 31 ॥
देशस्वामिपुरस्वामिपशुस्वामिपरिग्रहे ॥
मनुष्यपशुहस्त्यश्वधन वृद्धिकरी भव ॥ 32 ॥
अनेनैव विधानेन कार्या भूमिः समीक्षया ॥
द्वारन्यासं महाराज द्वारोच्छ्रायस्तथैव च ॥ 33 ॥
स्तम्भोच्छ्रायं तथा वंशविन्यासं च यदूत्तम ॥
तथामलकसारस्य चिह्नस्य तु समुच्छ्रयम् ॥34॥
आयुधं वाहनं चिह्नं यस्य देवस्य यद्भवेत्॥
तस्मादेकतमं चिह्नं कार्यं चामलसारके ॥ 35 ॥
3.19.m:
O Pūrṇā, offspring of Aṅgiras, make my desire fulfilled! / O Bhadrā, offspring of Kaśyapa, make my course auspicious!
Endowed with all seeds, surrounded by all gems and medicinal herbs, / delightful, gladdened, O Nandā, daughter of Vasiṣṭha, take delight here!
O daughter of Prajāpati, goddess, four-sided, made of earth, / fortunate, of good vows, auspicious one, O daughter of Kaśyapa, take delight here!
Unbroken, uninjured, full, daughter of the sage Aṅgiras! / O brick, grant my wish; I desire consecration!
O property of the lord of the country, the lord of the town, and the lord of cattle, / cause the increase of men, cattle, elephants, horses, and wealth!"
By this very rule the ground should be prepared, after careful inspection, / as well as the placement of the door, O great king, and the height of the door,
and the height of the pillars, and the arrangement of the beams, O best of the Yadus, / and likewise the erection of the emblem upon the āmalakasāra.
Whatever weapon, mount, or emblem belongs to whichever deity, / one among those emblems should be placed upon the āmalasāraka.

चित्रलक्षणवत्कार्यं सर्वकामसमृद्धिदम् ॥
आश्चर्याणि तथान्यानि तत्र यत्नान्निवेशयेत ॥ 37 ॥

वज्रं शक्रस्य कुर्वीत दण्डं वैवस्वतस्य च ॥
वरुणस्य तथा पाशं गदां च धनदस्य वै ॥ 41 ॥
स्कन्दस्य शक्तिः कर्तव्या गणाध्यक्षस्य पार्थिव ॥
कर्तव्यं परशोश्चिह्नं वह्नेर्ज्वाला विधीयते ॥ 42 ॥

एवं वादिनं श्रीभगवन्तममलतपसमतियश सञ्चिरजीविनं श्रीमार्कण्डेयं राजा वज्रः पप्रच्छ ।
भगवन्नष्टशल्यज्ञानं कथं भवति तमुवाच श्रीभगवान्मार्कण्डेयः ।
कदाचित्कमपि महद्भूतं त्रैलोक्यनाशायार्थितमभवत् ।
तद्भूतं ससंभ्रमैस्त्रिदशैर्निगृह्य वेगेनाधोमुखं न्यस्तम् ॥
तस्य चोत्थानभीता देवा अङ्गेषूपविष्टाः ।
तस्य पर्जन्याद्याः क्रमेण दक्षिणेऽङ्गभागे, व्युत्क्रमेण नागाद्या वामे, पर्जन्यहुताशनौ शिरसि, करग्रहौ वदने,दृशोश्च यज्ञकामौ, स्तनयोर्महेन्द्रादिती, श्रवणयोः रव्यदिती, उरःस्थले अंसयोश्च सत्यभृशान्तरिक्षपवनाः ।
भुजे चन्द्रभल्लाटमुख्या नागराजानः, द्वितीये भुजे सावित्रसवितारौ करौ रुद्रव्याधी द्वितीये करे, अर्यमा पृथिवीधरश्च करस्य कक्ष्ययोः, पुष्पवितथबहक्षताः पार्श्वे, शोषशोकयक्षाश्च द्वितीये पार्श्वे, हृदि ब्रह्मा, विवस्वान्मित्रश्च जठरे, जयेन्द्रौ मेढ्रे, वृषणयोश्च यमवरुणौ, स्फिजि वृषासुरौ, ऊर्वोः गन्धर्वपुष्पदन्तौ, जान्वोः मृगग्रीवौ। जङ्घयोः पितृदौवारिकौ चरणयोः, एवमयमेशानी दिक् शिरः नैरृती दिगादौ वास्तुपुरुषः ॥
तत्र च यत्स्वाङ्गं स्पृशप्रष्टा प्रयच्छति तत्रैव वास्त्वङ्गे शल्यं विद्यात् ।
अथवा यत्रैवाङ्गे गृहपतेः भूयोभूयो रुग्भवति ॥
अथ वास्तुदेवतामेकैकामुद्दिश्य घृतं जुहुयात् ।
यद्वाज्यं हूयमाने अग्निलक्षणमशरभं भवेत्तद्देवदेशे वा ॥
अथैतद्देवताभागे सुखेन शल्यज्ञानमहं चतुष्षष्टिपदविभागेन वक्ष्यामि ।
तत्र बहिः पूर्वेणार्धपदेश्वरः ।
पर्जन्यः अध्यर्धपदेश्वरः, पर्जन्यः अध्यर्धपदेश्वरकरग्रहः महेन्द्ररविसत्यवृषाः यथाक्रमं द्विद्विग्रहेशाः; अन्तरिक्षोध्यर्धपदेशः ।
पवनोऽर्धपदेशश्च दक्षिणेन पुष्पोऽर्धपदेशः ।
वितथोऽध्यर्धपदेशः ।
गृहर्क्षतयवभृङ्गगन्धर्वा द्विपदेशाः। कोशोऽध्यर्धपदेशः ।
शेषोऽर्धपदेशश्चात्र दिङ्नगराजेनार्धपदेशाः ।
मुख्योऽर्धपदेशः ।
भल्लाटचन्द्रादिदितयो द्विपदेशाः ।
रागोऽध्यर्धपदेशः ।
तदाशनोऽर्धपदेशश्च तदन्तरः पूर्वेणार्धपदनाथः ।
यक्षो द्विपदनाथोऽयं मा अर्धपदनाथः सावित्रो दक्षिणतोऽर्धपदनाथः सविता द्विपदनाथो मित्रः अर्धपदनाथो रुद्रः ।
उदगर्धपदनाथो व्याधिः ।
द्विपदनाथो महीश्वरः ।
अर्धपादनाथः कामः ।
मध्ये चतुष्पदेश्वरो ब्रह्मा एवं बहिर्द्वात्रिंशद्देवताः ।
अन्तस्त्रयोदश ।
एवं पञ्चचत्वारिंशत् ।
तत्र प्रश्नकाले ।
यस्य नाम श्रूयते रुतं वा तदस्ति विद्यात् पृच्छकवचनप्रथमाक्षराद्वा अकारादिवर्गे वाजिनराः श्वगोमायुमेषरासभाजम ।
वस्तुतो नवधा विभक्तस्य मध्ये वकारः अकनत एवं सग इत्येते क्रमेण प्राच्यादिषु वर्णाः ।
वर्णप्रथमश्रवणाद्वास्तुनि तद्दिशि शल्यम् ।
लग्नाच्छून्येषु केन्द्रेषु निःशल्यं दृढं भवति ।
पापयुक्तेषु सशल्यं च केन्द्रे राशिवशा दिग्भवति बलिनिग्रहे अस्थिशल्यम् ।
बलहीने शर्कराङ्गारकाष्ठतुषभस्मादि तत्र सर्वेष्वस्थिषु कर्तुर्मरणं भवति शर्करातुषकेशाङ्गारभस्मशल्येषु शोकानर्थव्याधिमरणचौरोपद्रवाः सशल्ये च देवतायतने देवतासन्निधानं न भवति ।
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन निःशल्यं वास्तुदैवतायतनं कुर्यात् ।
देवतायतनदक्षिणे भागे देवताकोशभवनम् ।
तस्याग्नेये महानसम् ।
दक्षिणेन स्नानभवनम ।
नैऋते कुप्यगृहम् ॥ ।
पश्चिमेन तोयगृहम ।
वायव्येन भाण्डगृहम् ।
उदक्प्रेक्ष्यागारम् ।
ऐशानेनेज्यागृहम् ।
प्राक्सर्वकर्मकारगृहमिति॥
एतान्यपि शल्यवर्जितानि कुर्यात् सर्वत्र द्रविणशल्येन वृद्धिर्भवति ।
तद्विज्ञानं भवति ।
भवति चात्र-
ऊर्द्ध्वस्थे केन्द्रगे सोम्यै शल्यं द्रविणसंज्ञितम्।

To the blessed one who was speaking thus, whose asceticism was stainless, whose fame was boundless, who lived for an aeon, the illustrious Mārkaṇḍeya, King Vajra asked:
"O venerable one, how is the knowledge of hidden extraneous substances determined?"
To him the blessed Mārkaṇḍeya said:
"Once, a great being sought the destruction of the three worlds.
Seizing that being in haste, the thirty [gods] threw him face down forcefully.
And afraid of his rising, the gods sat upon his limbs.
Upon his right bodily parts in order are Parjanya and others; in reverse order upon the left are the Nāgas and others; Parjanya and Hutāśana are on the head; Karagraha and [another] on the mouth; Yajña and Kāma on the two eyes; Mahendra and Aditi on the two breasts; Ravi and Aditi on the two ears; Satya, Bhṛśa, Antarikṣa, and Pavana on the chest and shoulders.
On one arm are the serpent kings headed by Candra and Bhallāṭa; on the second arm are Sāvitra and Savitṛ; Rudra and Vyādhi are on one hand, [and] on the second hand; Aryaman and Pṛthivīdhara are in the armpits; Puṣpa, Vitatha, and Bahukṣata are on the flank; Śoṣa, Śoka, and Yakṣa are on the second flank; Brahmā is in the heart; Vivasvat and Mitra are in the belly; Jayendra [and another] are in the penis; Yama and Varuṇa are in the testicles; Vṛṣa and Asura are on the buttocks; Gandharva and Puṣpadanta on the thighs; Mṛga and Grīva on the knees; Pitaraḥ and Dauvārika on the shanks; [and others] on the feet. Thus is this Vāstupuruṣa, with his head in the northeast direction and his feet in the southwest direction.
And there, whichever part of his own body the questioner touches, one should know that an extraneous substance is present precisely in that part of the site.
Or wherever on the body of the householder an illness repeatedly occurs.
Alternatively, one should offer clarified butter consecrated to each of the deities of the site.
Or where the characteristic of the fire becomes unfavorable while clarified butter is being offered, [the substance is] in that deity's place.
Now, I shall easily explain the knowledge of extraneous substances in the portion of these deities according to the division of sixty-four squares.
There, on the outside toward the east, is the lord of half a square.
Parjanya is the lord of one and a half squares; Karagraha is the lord of one and a half squares; Mahendra, Ravi, Satya, and Vṛṣa are respectively lords of two squares each; Antarikṣa is the lord of one and a half squares.
Pavana is the lord of half a square; and toward the south, Puṣpa is the lord of half a square.
Vitatha is the lord of one and a half squares.
Gṛharkṣata, Yava, Bhṛṅga, and Gandharva are lords of two squares; Kośa is the lord of one and a half squares.
Śeṣa is the lord of half a square, and here along with the serpent kings are lords of half a square.
Mukhya is the lord of half a square.
Bhallāṭa, Candra, and Aditi are lords of two squares.
Rāga is the lord of one and a half squares.
And Tadāśana is the lord of half a square, and between them toward the east is the lord of half a square.
Yakṣa is the lord of two squares; Aryaman is the lord of half a square; Sāvitra to the south is the lord of half a square; Savitṛ is the lord of two squares; Mitra is the lord of half a square; Rudra [is another].
To the north, Vyādhi is the lord of half a square.
Mahīśvara is the lord of two squares.
Kāma is the lord of half a square.
In the middle, Brahmā is the lord of four squares. Thus there are thirty-two deities on the outside.
There are thirteen inside.
Thus there are forty-five.
Now, at the time of questioning:
One should know that whichever [animal's] name is heard or whose cry is heard, it is present there; or from the first syllable of the questioner's speech: in the group of vowels beginning with 'a' are horse, man, dog, jackal, ram, donkey, and goat.
Of [the site] genuinely divided into nine parts, the letter 'va' is in the middle; 'a', 'ka', 'na', 'ta', 'sa', 'ga'—these letters are in order in the east and the other directions.
From the first hearing of a letter, an extraneous substance is in that direction of the site.
When the cardines are empty from the ascendant, it is firmly without any extraneous substance.
When joined with malefics, it has an extraneous substance; and in the cardine, the direction corresponds to the sign. When a planet is strong, there is a bone as the extraneous substance.
When it is weak, there are gravel, charcoal, wood, chaff, ash, and the like. There, among all of them, bones cause the death of the patron; when the extraneous substances are gravel, chaff, hair, charcoal, and ash, there are grief, disaster, illness, death, and distress from thieves; and when the temple of a deity has an extraneous substance, the presence of the deity does not take place.
Therefore, with every effort, one should make the site and the temple of the deity free of extraneous substances.
To the south of the temple of the deity is the treasury of the deity.
In its southeast is the kitchen.
To the south is the bathhouse.
In the southwest is the storehouse for base metals and household goods.
To the west is the waterhouse.
In the northwest is the storehouse for vessels.
To the north is the theater house.
In the northeast is the house for sacrifice.
To the east is the house for all workmen.
These also one should make free of extraneous substances; everywhere, an extraneous substance of treasure causes increase.
The recognition of it is as follows.
And here it is said:
When benefic planets are stationed aloft and located in a cardine, the extraneous substance is termed treasure;
the direction here too should be understood according to the sign in the cardine.

3.19.d:
ऊष्मा प्रदृश्यते यत्र च्छत्राकारः क्षितौ क्वचित् ।
तत्र वित्तं विजानीयात्सुषिरं यदि भूतलम्॥2॥
नीलाभिः श्वेतपक्ष्माभिर्मक्षिकाभिः समन्विता ॥
दुर्गन्धा च तथा भूमिस्तत्राधस्ताद्धनं भवेत् ॥ 3 ॥
एकनालसमर्थे द्वे दृश्येते यत्र पुष्करे ॥ ।
भूयोभूयश्च तत्राधः कथयन्ति धनं बहु ॥ 4 ॥
अक्षीरा क्षीरिणो वृक्षास्तन्तुभिर्यदि वेष्टिताः ॥
अकण्टकाः कण्टकिनस्तत्रापि द्रविणं वदेत् ॥5॥
द्रुमे भवति वंदाकं यत्र चान्यं नराधिप ॥ ॥
तत्रापि द्रविणं वाच्यं श्वेतं यत्र च किंशुकम् ॥ 6 ॥
हिमाम्भसी न ध्रियते न प्ररोहन्ति पादपाः ॥
अकाले पुप्पदा वृक्षास्तत्राधो धनमादिशेत ॥ 7 ॥
शाङ्गको मैथुनं यत्र भुजगश्चित्रमस्तकः ॥
दृश्यते यत्र राजेन्द्र तत्राधो धनमादिशेत ॥ 8 ॥
3.19.m:
Where warmth shaped like an umbrella is observed anywhere upon the earth, / there one should know wealth to be, if the ground is hollow.
Endowed with flies that have blue bodies and white eyelashes, / and likewise foul-smelling ground—underneath there will be wealth.
Where two lotuses capable [of blooming] upon a single stalk are seen, / they repeatedly say that much wealth lies underneath there.
If milky trees are without sap and wound about with filaments, / and thorny trees are thornless, there too one should declare treasure [to be].
Where mistletoe is found upon another tree, O king, / there too treasure should be declared, and where there is a white kiṃśuka tree.
Where frost and water are not retained, and trees do not sprout, / [yet] trees bear flowers out of season, there underneath one should indicate wealth.
Where copulation takes place, or a conch-headed serpent / with a variegated hood is seen, O king of kings, there underneath one should indicate wealth.

At what time should consecration be performed, O descendant of Bhṛgu? / Performed at which different times, what is it like then?

3.20.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Listen, I shall describe to you the time for performing consecration, / [and] how it turns out when performed at each various time, O Yādava.

3.20.s:
nityaṃ sannihitā loke vaiṣṇave ta yuge kṛtā ..
dhanadhānyavatī sphītā varadā ca tathā bhavet .. 3 ..

नित्यं सन्निहिता लोके वैष्णवे त युगे कृता ॥
धनधान्यवती स्फीता वरदा च तथा भवेत् ॥ 3 ॥
3.20.m: Ever present in the world, performed in the Vaiṣṇava age, / it will be rich in wealth and grain, thriving, and granter of boons.

3.20.s:
dṛṣṭā bhavati vikhyātā tridaśeśaguroryuge ..
aindre tejovatī sphītā bhūtanigrahakāriṇī ..4..
3.20.d:
दृष्टा भवति विख्याता त्रिदशेशगुरोर्युगे ॥
ऐन्द्रे तेजोवती स्फीता भूतनिग्रहकारिणी ॥4॥
3.20.m: In the [five-year] cycle of the teacher of the gods, it is seen to be renowned; / in Indra's, it is brilliant, prosperous, and restrains evil spirits.

3.20.s:
tathāvidhā tathāgneye bhūtadāhamavāpnuyāta ..
nityāścaryayutā tvāṣṭre gamyā lokaistathaiva ca .. 5 ..
3.20.d:
तथाविधा तथाग्नेये भूतदाहमवाप्नुयात ॥
नित्याश्चर्ययुता त्वाष्ट्रे गम्या लोकैस्तथैव च ॥ 5 ॥
3.20.m: Likewise in Agni's, it suffers burning by fire; / in Tvaṣṭṛ's, it is ever filled with wonder, and also approachable by the people.

3.20.s:
āhirbudhnye dṛḍhā nityaṃ lokānugrahakāriṇī ...
pitrye vināśamāpnoti kartuśca maraṇāvahā ..6..
3.20.d:
आहिर्बुध्न्ये दृढा नित्यं लोकानुग्रहकारिणी ॥।
पित्र्ये विनाशमाप्नोति कर्तुश्च मरणावहा ॥6॥
3.20.m: In Ahirbudhnya's, it is always firm and confers grace upon the people; / in the Ancestors', it meets with destruction and brings death to the patron.

3.20.s:
vaiśve lokahitā karturlokagamyā kṛtā bhaveta ..
saumyā saumye tathā kāntā varadā ca tathā bhavet .. 7 ..
3.20.d:
वैश्वे लोकहिता कर्तुर्लोकगम्या कृता भवेत ॥
सौम्या सौम्ये तथा कान्ता वरदा च तथा भवेत् ॥ 7 ॥
3.20.m: In the All-Gods' [cycle], when made, it is beneficial to the world and approachable by people; / in Soma's, it is gentle, lovely, and granter of boons.

3.20.s:
aindrāgne nāśamāpnoti kartuḥ kṛtvā vināśanam ..
aśvinī śrīmatī bhūtvā śīghraṃ nāśamavāpnuyāta .. 8 ..
3.20.d:
ऐन्द्राग्ने नाशमाप्नोति कर्तुः कृत्वा विनाशनम् ॥
अश्विनी श्रीमती भूत्वा शीघ्रं नाशमवाप्नुयात ॥ 8 ॥
3.20.m: In Indrāgni's, it meets destruction after causing the patron's destruction; / in the Aśvins', becoming prosperous, it quickly meets destruction.

3.20.s:
lokābhigamyā bhāgye syātkarturdoṃṣavatī bhaveta ..
aśubho'pi yuge kāryā pratiṣṭhā manujottama .. 9 ..
3.20.d:
लोकाभिगम्या भाग्ये स्यात्कर्तुर्दोंषवती भवेत ॥
अशुभोऽपि युगे कार्या प्रतिष्ठा मनुजोत्तम ॥ 9 ॥
3.20.m: In Bhaga's, it would be approachable by people, but brings faults upon the patron. / Even in an inauspicious cycle, an installation may be made, O best of men,

3.20.s:
yasminyasminyuge nātho yoyo devaḥ prakīrtitaḥ ..
dhanadhānyavatī sphītā kartuḥ śreyovahā tathā .. 3.96.10 ..
3.20.d:
यस्मिन्यस्मिन्युगे नाथो योयो देवः प्रकीर्तितः ॥
धनधान्यवती स्फीता कर्तुः श्रेयोवहा तथा ॥ 3.96.10 ॥

3.20.s:
saṃvatsarākhye kartavyā nityamājñāyutā bhaveta ..

3.20.m: In [the year] named Saṃvatsara it should be made; it will always possess authority; / in Parivatsara, it slays evil spirits and is renowned in the world;

3.20.s:
iḍāpūrve tathā saumyā varadā lokasundarī ..

अनुपूर्वे तु वरदा धनधान्यवती भवेत्। 12॥
3.20.m: in Iḍāvatsara, it is gentle, granting boons, and fair to the world; / in Anuvatsara, it is granting boons, possessed of wealth and grain.

3.20.s:

धनधान्ययुता स्फीता लोकानन्दकरी भवेत्॥ 14॥
3.20.m: In the northern solstice, it is gentle and increases wealth; / filled with wealth and grain, prosperous, and causes joy to the people.

3.20.s:
dakṣiṇe tvayane kartuḥ pāpavṛddhikarī bhavet ..
tatrāpi supte deveśe sarvānarthavivarddhinī .. 15 ..
3.20.d:
